key_insight: PixelSmile disentangles overlapping facial expression semantics using a fully symmetric joint training diffusion framework and a continuous affect dataset, enabling fine-grained, controllable expression edits while preserving identity. This combination plus a targeted benchmark reduces structural confusion and improves linear controllability of edits.
problem_solved: Overcoming intrinsic semantic overlap in facial expressions that causes structural confusion and poor fine-grained control in expression editing methods, and the lack of continuous annotated data and benchmarks to evaluate these behaviors.
method: Construct FFE (Flex Facial Expression) dataset with continuous affective annotations to capture fine-grained expression variation.
Establish FFE-Bench to measure structural confusion, editing accuracy, linear controllability, and the trade-off between expression editing and identity preservation.
Introduce PixelSmile: a diffusion-based editing framework that uses fully symmetric joint training to disentangle expression semantics and enable precise, identity-preserving edits.
impact: Provides practitioners with a new dataset, benchmark, and model that enable precise, controllable facial expression editing—useful for animation, AR/VR avatars, affective computing, and data augmentation—while making evaluation of fine-grained edits more reliable.
visual_elements: Dataset visualization: 2D scatter of faces in continuous affect space (valence/arousal or learned embedding) showing dense, continuous annotations.
Model diagram: schematic of PixelSmile diffusion pipeline with 'fully symmetric joint training' blocks and disentanglement pathways.
Benchmark radar chart: comparison of structural confusion, editing accuracy, linear controllability, and identity preservation across methods.
Before/after gallery: image triplets (original, target expression control slider, edited result) demonstrating fine-grained, identity-preserving edits.
paper_title: PixelSmile: Toward Fine-Grained Facial Expression Editing
paper_authors: Jiabin Hua, Hengyuan Xu, Aojie Li, Wei Cheng, Gang Yu
